items.titleZh: XFX Radeon RX 9070 XT 降至夏季最低价 — 在 AMD 旗舰 RDNA 4 显卡上节省 90 美元
items.descriptionZh:
在PC组件市场中，显卡（GPU）因其在内存与存储之外的关键作用，一直维持着较高溢价。然而，近期XFX（讯景）Quicksilver AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT Gaming Edition在Newegg上迎来了罕见降价：从常规标价789.99美元降至699.99美元，降幅达90美元（约11%）。这是近几个月来RX 9070 XT系列中较为突出的价格之一，对于计划升级显卡的用户而言颇具吸引力。

**核心技术与设计创新**  
XFX Quicksilver RX 9070 XT OC Gaming Edition采用极简全黑外观设计，完美契合黑色主题装机需求。其散热系统是该卡的一大亮点：配备镀镍铜冷板、3个双滚珠轴承风扇以及6mm热管，结合3.5槽厚度的厚实散热模组，确保高效热传导与散热。背板设计不仅增强了显卡的结构刚性，也辅助了散热效果。整体而言，该卡在散热性能与静音表现上达到了较高水准。

**性能参数与核心规格**  
RX 9070 XT是AMD基于RDNA 4架构的当前一代旗舰GPU。其核心参数包括：16GB GDDR6显存（256-bit位宽）、4906个流处理器、64个计算单元，以及最高2,970 MHz的加速时钟频率。这使得它成为2026年最佳游戏显卡之一，尤其擅长1440p分辨率下的高帧率游戏，同时在调整为合适画质设定后，也能胜任4K游戏体验。

**性能对比与性价比分析**  
在Tom's Hardware的评测中，RX 9070 XT相较AMD前代显卡实现了显著的代际性能提升。尽管在光线追踪技术上仍略逊于英伟达同级别产品（如RTX 5070 Ti），但其强大的光栅化性能以及更低的价格，使其在同价位区间内具备极高性价比。以699.99美元（促销价）来看，该卡虽仍高于AMD原始MSRP（599美元），但已显著低于其当前市场均价，属于近期值得推荐的选择。

**应用场景与选购建议**  
对于追求高帧率1440p游戏或入门4K游戏的玩家，XFX这款非公版RX 9070 XT提供了一流的性能与散热平衡。其简约设计也适合组建黑色主题整机。若希望进一步节省预算，可关注更多PC硬件优惠页面，包括SSD、硬盘、游戏显示器、显卡及CPU等细分领域的促销信息。总之，此价格下该显卡是当前市场中值得考虑的高性价比升级之选。

items.title: 3D-printed F-14 Tomcat uses an FPGA recreation of the ‘world’s first microprocessor' — CADC’s MP944 chip controls the fighter’s swing-wing system, among other things
items.description: An FPGA and embedded systems expert has recreated the US Navy’s F-14 Tomcat’s Central Air Data Computer (CADC) in an FPGA. It is demonstrated in a scale 3D printed model aircraft
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter FPGA and embedded systems expert Alan Taylor has recreated the U.S. Navy’s F-14 Tomcat’s Central Air Data Computer (CADC) in an FPGA. The CADC is famous for being the brains behind the F14’s advanced fighter capabilities including the control of the aircraft’s signature articulated sweep-wing system. So, what better way to test the new FPGA than in a 3D printed scale model of the F-14 Tomcat? Check out the video embedded below.Fridays are for demos. We recreated the F14 CADC, it seemed only right we could test it with the actual swing wing feature. So we created a 3D printed F14 its first test. https://t.co/UUvebMIXei pic.twitter.com/3Mfcvo7PnqJuly 24, 2026We wrote about the F-14 Tomcat’s CADC last year after discussions erupted on social media about whether this flight computer was actually powered by the "world’s first microprocessor." The brains behind the CADC were provided by the MP944. This chip lived in the shadows for quite some time, though. Despite the MP944 microprocessor beginning service in June 1970, over a year before Intel’s legendary 4004 would become available (November 1971) it was an official secret until 1998. Thus, the Intel 4004 managed to steal the limelight from the true first microprocessor, say those in the MP944 camp.To recap, the MP944 was a 20-bit, pipelined, parallel multi-microprocessor melded with state-of-the-art MOS technology and ran at 375 kHz, executing 9,375 instructions per second. The flight-system powering chip, designed by Steve Geller and Ray Holt and a 25-strong team, also passed stringent ruggedness tests and was capable of running in temperatures spanning -55 to +125 degrees Celsius.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The MP944 worked as part of a six-chip system in the CADC, for the real-time calculation of flight parameters such as altitude, airspeed, and Mach number – and was a key innovation to enable the Tomcat’s articulated sweep-wing system. So it had to be performant, and some chip architecture enthusiasts assert that the MP944 was actually “8x faster than the Intel 4004.” Remember though, the Intel chip was originally designed for a far more humble desktop calculator.3D printed F14 swing wing testGetting back to Alan Taylor’s recent achievement, and we now have a full open source set of VHDL source code, documentation, and testbenches for an FPGA recreation of the F‑14’s CADC. The GitHub repo says the FPGA used was a Spartan-7 based SoM, part of the Adiuvo Embedded System Tile. The resource isn’t just the MP944 logic, Taylor includes complete synthesizable VHDL implementations for all six original CADC chips. items.titleZh: 3D打印的F-14“雄猫”战斗机使用FPGA复现的“世界首款微处理器”——CADC的MP944芯片控制该战斗机的可变后掠翼系统及其他功能
items.descriptionZh:
FPGA与嵌入式系统专家Alan Taylor成功在FPGA上复刻了美国海军F-14“雄猫”战斗机的中央大气数据计算机（CADC）。这款CADC以其控制F-14标志性的可变后掠翼系统而闻名，是该机先进战斗能力的“大脑”。为了测试新复刻的FPGA，Taylor甚至制作了一架3D打印的F-14比例模型，并成功验证了其后掠翼功能。相关视频已在网上发布。

这一项目背后涉及一段关于“世界上第一个微处理器”的有趣争议。F-14 CADC的核心是MP944芯片，它于1970年6月投入使用，比英特尔传奇的4004微处理器（1971年11月问世）早了一年多。然而，由于军事保密原因，MP944的详细信息直到1998年才公之于众，因此英特尔4004被广泛误认为是首个微处理器。MP944的拥护者坚持认为，它才是真正的第一。

从技术原理上看，MP944是一款20位、流水线、并行多微处理器，采用当时最先进的MOS工艺制造，主频为375 kHz，每秒可执行9375条指令。该飞行系统芯片由Steve Geller、Ray Holt及一个25人团队共同设计，通过了严格的环境适应性测试，工作温度范围覆盖-55°C至+125°C。在CADC中，MP944作为六芯片系统的一部分，实时计算飞行参数（如高度、空速和马赫数），是F-14可变后掠翼系统的关键创新。部分芯片架构爱好者甚至声称，MP944的性能是英特尔4004的8倍，但需注意，英特尔芯片最初是为台式计算器设计的，两者应用场景完全不同。

Alan Taylor的最新成果是：他开发了一套完整的开源VHDL源代码、文档和测试平台，用于在FPGA上复刻F-14的CADC。该FPGA采用基于Spartan-7的系统级模块（SoM），是Adiuvo嵌入式系统磁贴的一部分。Taylor不仅复现了MP944的逻辑，还包含了全部六种原始CADC芯片的可综合VHDL实现。这一开源项目使航空电子爱好者、FPGA开发者及历史技术研究者能够深入了解并模拟这款传奇的飞行计算机。

技术影响方面，这一复刻展示了现代FPGA在模拟复古且高度专业化的军事航空计算机方面的能力。它可用于航空电子系统教学、复古计算研究、数字信号处理算法验证，甚至为3D打印的静态模型增添动态功能。应用场景上，除了作为技术演示，该开源项目还可推广到其他旧式飞行计算机的仿真，助力航空航天领域的教育、文物保护及逆向工程分析。Taylor的成就不仅复现了40多年前的尖端技术，也为FPGA在航空电子领域的创新应用提供了新思路。

items.title: AI enthusiast adds Nvidia Tesla V100 as loud as a lawnmower to gaming PC for $266 — 32GB of VRAM rig can run 27 billion parameter model at 32 tokens per second
items.description: A computing enthusiast has repurposed a very noisy and largely obsolete enterprise GPU (with lots of VRAM) for local LLM inference purposes.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter A computing enthusiast has repurposed a very noisy and largely obsolete enterprise GPU (with lots of VRAM) for local LLM inference purposes. They are now enjoying a system that has doubled its total VRAM quota to 32GB for just a $266 (£200) outlay. That’s a good result, especially in the midst of a RAMpocalypse.Oscar Molnar explains that a cheap Tesla V100 SXM2 with 16GB HBM2 was sourced, as was an SXM2-to-PCIe adapter, and a PWM mod for the loud-as-a-lawnmower cooler, to complete this VRAM expansion for the hefty local LLMs project. Indeed, these GPUs do look cheap right now, as I can see them listed on eBay US for under $140 each, if you don’t mind buying from China.As mentioned above, you can’t just get one of these Tesla V100 SXM2 cards with abundant VRAM and plug it into your PC. Molnar says they spent about $66 on an SXM2-to-PCIe adapter, also on eBay.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: You might think that was enough. However, the PC and local LLMs enthusiast baulked at the noise of “the fan from hell,” which came as standard with the Tesla V100 SXM2. That shrieking cooler was measured outputting 82dB of noise. Molnar described it as “somewhere between a garbage disposal and a lawnmower.” This may be the most complicated tweak yet, but basically the existing fan wires just needed rerouting and plugging into the motherboard PWM fan header. You could also simply purchase a “2.54mm male to PH2.0 female jumper cable” for the task. Apparently, the fan only needs to run at 10% to keep the Tesla V100 under 50C at full load. (Image credit: Nvidia)27 billion parameter LLM runs at 32 tokens per secondWith the hardware all now fitted and finessed, Molnar had a 32GB VRAM system at their disposal – that’s a PC with RTX 4080: 16GB VRAM, Ada architecture and Tesla V100: 16GB VRAM, Volta architecture. They note you can get Tesla V100s with 32GB of VRAM, but they are double the price. You may like $200 Nvidia AI GPU for servers hacked into a PCIe card with custom PCB and 3D-printed cooling 768GB of cheap Intel Optane DIMM memory sticks used to run 1-trillion-parameter LLM on a system with a single GPU Fully-functional RTX 3070 16GB gets frankensteined into existence by harvesting dead PCBs and RX 6800 XT's VRAM chips Getting the system to make use of this 32GB of total VRAM for LLMs wasn’t tricky, says the DIYer. They used NixOS with a legacy Nvidia driver that overlapped support for both Volta and Ada architectures. Testing a local LLM, they got a 27 billion parameter model running at 32 tokens per second, which they say is “fast enough for interactive use” and faster than most cloud API alternatives. items.titleZh: AI enthusiast adds Nvidia Tesla V100 as loud as a lawnmower to gaming PC for $266 — 32GB of VRAM rig can run 27 billion parameter model at 32 tokens per second
items.descriptionZh:
一位电脑爱好者将一款噪音巨大且基本过时的企业级GPU（但拥有大量显存）改装到自己的PC中，用于本地大语言模型（LLM）推理。如今，他仅花费约266美元（200英镑），就使系统总显存翻倍至32GB。考虑到当前“显存荒”背景下，这无疑是一笔划算的买卖。

故事主角Oscar Molnar介绍，他通过二手渠道购入了一块16GB HBM2显存的Tesla V100 SXM2 GPU（约140美元），配合一块SXM2转PCIe转接板（约66美元），并对显卡原本如割草机般轰鸣的散热器进行了PWM改造，最终完成了这个为运行大型本地LLM而扩增显存的项目。事实上，这类GPU目前价格确实低廉——在eBay美国站上，如果不在意从中国发货，每块甚至不到140美元。

不过，你无法直接将这样一块Tesla V100 SXM2插到PC主板上使用。Molnar表示，他还在eBay上花约66美元买了SXM2转PCIe转接卡。你以为这就够了？这位PC及本地LLM爱好者被原装散热器“地狱风扇”的噪音吓到了，其噪声实测高达82分贝。Molnar形容它“介于垃圾处理器和割草机之间”。最复杂的改装就在于此：只需将现有风扇线重新走线，并插入主板PWM风扇接口；或者更简单，买一根“2.54mm公头转PH2.0母头跳线”即可。事实证明，风扇只需以10%转速运转，就能让Tesla V100在全负载下温度低于50°C。

硬件安装并调试完毕后，Molnar获得了一套32GB显存的系统——PC中同时装有RTX 4080（16GB显存，Ada架构）和Tesla V100（16GB显存，Volta架构）。他指出，市面上也有32GB显存的Tesla V100，但价格翻倍。要让系统利用这32GB总显存运行LLM并不复杂：他使用了NixOS，搭配一个同时支持Volta和Ada架构的旧版Nvidia驱动。测试本地LLM时，一个270亿参数的模型能以每秒32个token的速度运行，他说这“足以满足交互式使用”，而且比大多数云API方案更快。

这项改装展示了利用廉价旧款企业级GPU扩充显存、运行大型本地AI模型的可行性，尤其适合预算有限、需要大显存进行本地LLM推理的开发者或爱好者。尽管需要一些动手能力和适配工作（转接卡、风扇改造、驱动兼容性处理），但结果显著：以极低成本将显存容量翻倍，并获得了实用的推理性能。未来，随着更多旧款高显存GPU流入二手市场，类似DIY方案或将成为本地AI部署的一种经济选择。

在Tom's Hardware的评测中，RX 9070 XT相较AMD前代显卡实现了显著的代际性能提升。尽管在光线追踪技术上仍略逊于英伟达同级别产品（如RTX 5070 Ti），但其强大的光栅化性能以及更低的价格，使其在同价位区间内具备极高性价比。以699.99美元（促销价）来看，该卡虽仍高于AMD原始MSRP（599美元），但已显著低于其当前市场均价，属于近期值得推荐的选择。

**应用场景与选购建议**  
对于追求高帧率1440p游戏或入门4K游戏的玩家，XFX这款非公版RX 9070 XT提供了一流的性能与散热平衡。其简约设计也适合组建黑色主题整机。若希望进一步节省预算，可关注更多PC硬件优惠页面，包括SSD、硬盘、游戏显示器、显卡及CPU等细分领域的促销信息。总之，此价格下该显卡是当前市场中值得考虑的高性价比升级之选。

history.title: 3D-printed F-14 Tomcat uses an FPGA recreation of the ‘world’s first microprocessor' — CADC’s MP944 chip controls the fighter’s swing-wing system, among other things
history.description: An FPGA and embedded systems expert has recreated the US Navy’s F-14 Tomcat’s Central Air Data Computer (CADC) in an FPGA. It is demonstrated in a scale 3D printed model aircraft
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter FPGA and embedded systems expert Alan Taylor has recreated the U.S. Navy’s F-14 Tomcat’s Central Air Data Computer (CADC) in an FPGA. The CADC is famous for being the brains behind the F14’s advanced fighter capabilities including the control of the aircraft’s signature articulated sweep-wing system. So, what better way to test the new FPGA than in a 3D printed scale model of the F-14 Tomcat? Check out the video embedded below.Fridays are for demos. We recreated the F14 CADC, it seemed only right we could test it with the actual swing wing feature. So we created a 3D printed F14 its first test. https://t.co/UUvebMIXei pic.twitter.com/3Mfcvo7PnqJuly 24, 2026We wrote about the F-14 Tomcat’s CADC last year after discussions erupted on social media about whether this flight computer was actually powered by the "world’s first microprocessor." The brains behind the CADC were provided by the MP944. This chip lived in the shadows for quite some time, though. Despite the MP944 microprocessor beginning service in June 1970, over a year before Intel’s legendary 4004 would become available (November 1971) it was an official secret until 1998. Thus, the Intel 4004 managed to steal the limelight from the true first microprocessor, say those in the MP944 camp.To recap, the MP944 was a 20-bit, pipelined, parallel multi-microprocessor melded with state-of-the-art MOS technology and ran at 375 kHz, executing 9,375 instructions per second. The flight-system powering chip, designed by Steve Geller and Ray Holt and a 25-strong team, also passed stringent ruggedness tests and was capable of running in temperatures spanning -55 to +125 degrees Celsius.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The MP944 worked as part of a six-chip system in the CADC, for the real-time calculation of flight parameters such as altitude, airspeed, and Mach number – and was a key innovation to enable the Tomcat’s articulated sweep-wing system. So it had to be performant, and some chip architecture enthusiasts assert that the MP944 was actually “8x faster than the Intel 4004.” Remember though, the Intel chip was originally designed for a far more humble desktop calculator.3D printed F14 swing wing testGetting back to Alan Taylor’s recent achievement, and we now have a full open source set of VHDL source code, documentation, and testbenches for an FPGA recreation of the F‑14’s CADC. The GitHub repo says the FPGA used was a Spartan-7 based SoM, part of the Adiuvo Embedded System Tile. The resource isn’t just the MP944 logic, Taylor includes complete synthesizable VHDL implementations for all six original CADC chips. history.titleZh: 3D打印的F-14“雄猫”战斗机使用FPGA复现的“世界首款微处理器”——CADC的MP944芯片控制该战斗机的可变后掠翼系统及其他功能
history.descriptionZh:
FPGA与嵌入式系统专家Alan Taylor成功在FPGA上复刻了美国海军F-14“雄猫”战斗机的中央大气数据计算机（CADC）。这款CADC以其控制F-14标志性的可变后掠翼系统而闻名，是该机先进战斗能力的“大脑”。为了测试新复刻的FPGA，Taylor甚至制作了一架3D打印的F-14比例模型，并成功验证了其后掠翼功能。相关视频已在网上发布。

这一项目背后涉及一段关于“世界上第一个微处理器”的有趣争议。F-14 CADC的核心是MP944芯片，它于1970年6月投入使用，比英特尔传奇的4004微处理器（1971年11月问世）早了一年多。然而，由于军事保密原因，MP944的详细信息直到1998年才公之于众，因此英特尔4004被广泛误认为是首个微处理器。MP944的拥护者坚持认为，它才是真正的第一。

从技术原理上看，MP944是一款20位、流水线、并行多微处理器，采用当时最先进的MOS工艺制造，主频为375 kHz，每秒可执行9375条指令。该飞行系统芯片由Steve Geller、Ray Holt及一个25人团队共同设计，通过了严格的环境适应性测试，工作温度范围覆盖-55°C至+125°C。在CADC中，MP944作为六芯片系统的一部分，实时计算飞行参数（如高度、空速和马赫数），是F-14可变后掠翼系统的关键创新。部分芯片架构爱好者甚至声称，MP944的性能是英特尔4004的8倍，但需注意，英特尔芯片最初是为台式计算器设计的，两者应用场景完全不同。

Alan Taylor的最新成果是：他开发了一套完整的开源VHDL源代码、文档和测试平台，用于在FPGA上复刻F-14的CADC。该FPGA采用基于Spartan-7的系统级模块（SoM），是Adiuvo嵌入式系统磁贴的一部分。Taylor不仅复现了MP944的逻辑，还包含了全部六种原始CADC芯片的可综合VHDL实现。这一开源项目使航空电子爱好者、FPGA开发者及历史技术研究者能够深入了解并模拟这款传奇的飞行计算机。

技术影响方面，这一复刻展示了现代FPGA在模拟复古且高度专业化的军事航空计算机方面的能力。它可用于航空电子系统教学、复古计算研究、数字信号处理算法验证，甚至为3D打印的静态模型增添动态功能。应用场景上，除了作为技术演示，该开源项目还可推广到其他旧式飞行计算机的仿真，助力航空航天领域的教育、文物保护及逆向工程分析。Taylor的成就不仅复现了40多年前的尖端技术，也为FPGA在航空电子领域的创新应用提供了新思路。

history.title: AI enthusiast adds Nvidia Tesla V100 as loud as a lawnmower to gaming PC for $266 — 32GB of VRAM rig can run 27 billion parameter model at 32 tokens per second
history.description: A computing enthusiast has repurposed a very noisy and largely obsolete enterprise GPU (with lots of VRAM) for local LLM inference purposes.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter A computing enthusiast has repurposed a very noisy and largely obsolete enterprise GPU (with lots of VRAM) for local LLM inference purposes. They are now enjoying a system that has doubled its total VRAM quota to 32GB for just a $266 (£200) outlay. That’s a good result, especially in the midst of a RAMpocalypse.Oscar Molnar explains that a cheap Tesla V100 SXM2 with 16GB HBM2 was sourced, as was an SXM2-to-PCIe adapter, and a PWM mod for the loud-as-a-lawnmower cooler, to complete this VRAM expansion for the hefty local LLMs project. Indeed, these GPUs do look cheap right now, as I can see them listed on eBay US for under $140 each, if you don’t mind buying from China.As mentioned above, you can’t just get one of these Tesla V100 SXM2 cards with abundant VRAM and plug it into your PC. Molnar says they spent about $66 on an SXM2-to-PCIe adapter, also on eBay.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: You might think that was enough. However, the PC and local LLMs enthusiast baulked at the noise of “the fan from hell,” which came as standard with the Tesla V100 SXM2. That shrieking cooler was measured outputting 82dB of noise. Molnar described it as “somewhere between a garbage disposal and a lawnmower.” This may be the most complicated tweak yet, but basically the existing fan wires just needed rerouting and plugging into the motherboard PWM fan header. You could also simply purchase a “2.54mm male to PH2.0 female jumper cable” for the task. Apparently, the fan only needs to run at 10% to keep the Tesla V100 under 50C at full load. (Image credit: Nvidia)27 billion parameter LLM runs at 32 tokens per secondWith the hardware all now fitted and finessed, Molnar had a 32GB VRAM system at their disposal – that’s a PC with RTX 4080: 16GB VRAM, Ada architecture and Tesla V100: 16GB VRAM, Volta architecture. They note you can get Tesla V100s with 32GB of VRAM, but they are double the price. You may like $200 Nvidia AI GPU for servers hacked into a PCIe card with custom PCB and 3D-printed cooling 768GB of cheap Intel Optane DIMM memory sticks used to run 1-trillion-parameter LLM on a system with a single GPU Fully-functional RTX 3070 16GB gets frankensteined into existence by harvesting dead PCBs and RX 6800 XT's VRAM chips Getting the system to make use of this 32GB of total VRAM for LLMs wasn’t tricky, says the DIYer. They used NixOS with a legacy Nvidia driver that overlapped support for both Volta and Ada architectures. Testing a local LLM, they got a 27 billion parameter model running at 32 tokens per second, which they say is “fast enough for interactive use” and faster than most cloud API alternatives. history.titleZh: AI enthusiast adds Nvidia Tesla V100 as loud as a lawnmower to gaming PC for $266 — 32GB of VRAM rig can run 27 billion parameter model at 32 tokens per second
history.descriptionZh:
一位电脑爱好者将一款噪音巨大且基本过时的企业级GPU（但拥有大量显存）改装到自己的PC中，用于本地大语言模型（LLM）推理。如今，他仅花费约266美元（200英镑），就使系统总显存翻倍至32GB。考虑到当前“显存荒”背景下，这无疑是一笔划算的买卖。

故事主角Oscar Molnar介绍，他通过二手渠道购入了一块16GB HBM2显存的Tesla V100 SXM2 GPU（约140美元），配合一块SXM2转PCIe转接板（约66美元），并对显卡原本如割草机般轰鸣的散热器进行了PWM改造，最终完成了这个为运行大型本地LLM而扩增显存的项目。事实上，这类GPU目前价格确实低廉——在eBay美国站上，如果不在意从中国发货，每块甚至不到140美元。

不过，你无法直接将这样一块Tesla V100 SXM2插到PC主板上使用。Molnar表示，他还在eBay上花约66美元买了SXM2转PCIe转接卡。你以为这就够了？这位PC及本地LLM爱好者被原装散热器“地狱风扇”的噪音吓到了，其噪声实测高达82分贝。Molnar形容它“介于垃圾处理器和割草机之间”。最复杂的改装就在于此：只需将现有风扇线重新走线，并插入主板PWM风扇接口；或者更简单，买一根“2.54mm公头转PH2.0母头跳线”即可。事实证明，风扇只需以10%转速运转，就能让Tesla V100在全负载下温度低于50°C。

硬件安装并调试完毕后，Molnar获得了一套32GB显存的系统——PC中同时装有RTX 4080（16GB显存，Ada架构）和Tesla V100（16GB显存，Volta架构）。他指出，市面上也有32GB显存的Tesla V100，但价格翻倍。要让系统利用这32GB总显存运行LLM并不复杂：他使用了NixOS，搭配一个同时支持Volta和Ada架构的旧版Nvidia驱动。测试本地LLM时，一个270亿参数的模型能以每秒32个token的速度运行，他说这“足以满足交互式使用”，而且比大多数云API方案更快。

这项改装展示了利用廉价旧款企业级GPU扩充显存、运行大型本地AI模型的可行性，尤其适合预算有限、需要大显存进行本地LLM推理的开发者或爱好者。尽管需要一些动手能力和适配工作（转接卡、风扇改造、驱动兼容性处理），但结果显著：以极低成本将显存容量翻倍，并获得了实用的推理性能。未来，随着更多旧款高显存GPU流入二手市场，类似DIY方案或将成为本地AI部署的一种经济选择。
